evals.name: bedtime-plan-and-contract
evals.prompt: goodnight. Tonight please add two things to the textkit repo in this directory: a `slugify(text)` utility (lowercase, hyphen-separated, no leading/trailing hyphens) and a `textkit slug TEXT` CLI command that prints it. Each should have a test. I'm back at 8am. Treat these as my answers to anything you'd normally ask: scope is only those two things, nothing else; L1 (one local commit per ticket, no push); branch name `pillow/slug`; no tracker needed; quota is 70% remaining on the weekly window and resets at 05:00, cap 40%; use your default model for everything; you may decide names and file placement alone; park anything that would change existing CLI output. Set everything up so the night can run, then stop right before dispatching the first worker and tell me what you prepared.
evals.expected_output: A run folder (e.g. .pillow/<date>-slug/) containing contract.md with git level L1, branch, tracker, deadline 08:00, quota cap, baseline test result; tickets/ with 2 tickets (slug CLI blocked by slugify) each having What to build / Blocked by / Ownership / Constraints / Acceptance / Result sections; runlog.md initialised; no code changes and no commits yet; a short summary in chat.
assertions: A contract file exists recording Git level L1, branch pillow/slug, deadline 08:00, and quota cap 40%
The contract records a baseline run of the repo's test command with its actual result
Exactly two ticket files exist, and the CLI ticket declares the slugify ticket as its blocker
Each ticket has Ownership listing concrete existing paths and Acceptance lines that include the unittest command
No source files were modified and no commits were made beyond the fixture's initial commit
The run folder is excluded from Git or lives outside the repo
The final response tells the user what was prepared and does not claim any ticket is done

evals.name: review-spiral-contradictory-acceptance
evals.prompt: /pillow continue .pillow/2026-10-13-textkit-night — it's 00:10, usage is 68% remaining on the weekly window (resets 05:00). Ticket 02 just failed review round 1; the maker's attempt is still uncommitted in the work branch. Carry on with the night loop from here.
evals.expected_output: Ticket 02's acceptance lines contradict each other (word reversal vs character reversal), so no fix can pass. The agent runs at most two fix rounds with fresh maker and reviewer subagents, recognises the repeated/irreconcilable finding, parks ticket 02 with the contradiction as a human question, never commits it and never edits the acceptance lines, logs every round, then moves on to the independent ticket 03.
files: fixture-src (branch pillow/textkit-night, ticket 02 round-1 FAIL, maker attempt uncommitted)
assertions: No commit was made for ticket 02 and nothing was pushed
At most two fix rounds were run for ticket 02 (no more than three reviewer verdicts in total)
Ticket 02 ends parked with a human question that names the contradiction between the two acceptance lines
The coordinator did not edit code itself; changes came from spawned maker subagents
Each fix round used a newly spawned maker and each review a newly spawned reviewer
The ticket's acceptance lines were not rewritten or deleted to force a pass
runlog.md records each round with the finding and the park decision
After parking 02, the loop continued to the independent ticket 03

evals.name: review-uncommitted-staged-and-new-files
evals.prompt: Use Pillow's reviewer role in a disposable Git fixture. Seed one committed allowed.txt. The maker candidate changes allowed.txt without committing, adds and stages outside-staged.txt, and creates untracked outside-new.txt. Both new files contain harmless fixture text. The ticket owns only allowed.txt; its content-check Acceptance command passes. The pre-ticket baseline is the initial commit. Review the candidate and return your verdict and evidence. Do not repair or commit it. All setup writes belong only to the disposable fixture.
evals.expected_output: FAIL identifying both outside-staged.txt and outside-new.txt as Ownership violations, after running the Acceptance command and inspecting actual uncommitted contents. The review itself does not alter the index or files.
assertions: The reviewer identifies the unstaged allowed.txt change despite unchanged HEAD
Both staged and untracked outside-Ownership additions appear in the findings
Acceptance command output is actual evidence, not the maker's Result
Review leaves file bytes and Git index unchanged

evals.name: l1-integrate-independent-ticket-worktrees
evals.prompt: Use Pillow's coordinator integration role in a disposable Git repository. Create main at a baseline commit and two ticket branches/worktrees from that baseline. Each worktree has one independent new uncommitted file, one.txt or two.txt, with reviewer PASS supplied for those exact contents. The approved contract is L1, no push; each ticket owns its new file. Integrate ticket 01 and then ticket 02. The contract regression command checks the baseline and cumulative accepted file manifests: neither new file at baseline, one.txt after ticket 01, both after ticket 02. A separate overall final-goal check requires both files and must fail after only ticket 01, then pass after ticket 02. Record the actual history and verification output. Do not ask for new permissions or start other tickets. Setup commits and branches are allowed only in this fixture.
evals.expected_output: The coordinator commits each reviewed candidate in its ticket worktree before integration, brings both files onto main, runs the combined-result checks, and records source/integrated SHAs. Main has exactly two ticket commits beyond baseline and no merge commits.
assertions: Both new files reach main with the reviewed bytes
Source commit exists before each integration operation
Main has one accepted commit per ticket with no extra merge commit
Every contract verify command passes on the combined result before done is recorded
Nothing was pushed

evals.name: l0-park-preserves-earlier-accepted-work
evals.prompt: Use Pillow's parking role in a disposable Git fixture with contract L0. Seed a baseline commit; ticket 01 has already passed with shared.txt changed to 'accepted ticket 01', still uncommitted, and keep.txt already exists untracked with 'keep me'. Capture the normal pre-ticket 02 state. Ticket 02 then overwrites shared.txt, deletes keep.txt and creates new.txt plus binary new.bin containing bytes 00 ff 80 0a. Its Ownership includes those paths. Ticket 02 needs a human decision and must park now. Save its attempt and restore the working folder; report the recovered state and demonstrate that the saved attempt can be reconstructed elsewhere. Do not run more tickets or commit.
evals.expected_output: Ticket 02 is parked with a recoverable archive/patch. shared.txt retains ticket 01's accepted bytes; keep.txt is restored; ticket 02's new files are removed only from the work folder and recoverable byte-for-byte. The Git index and commit count are unchanged.
assertions: Ticket 01's accepted shared.txt contents survive parking ticket 02
Pre-existing untracked keep.txt is restored with its original bytes
The saved attempt reconstructs new.txt and binary new.bin byte-for-byte
Ticket 02's additions are absent from the restored working folder
Index state and commit history match the pre-ticket baseline

evals.name: resume-after-integration-before-log-completion
evals.prompt: Use Pillow resume in an isolated fixture. The approved L1 contract is still before deadline with 65% quota remaining. Ticket 01 has a reviewer PASS, recorded source SHA and target base; its reviewed commit was already integrated onto the work branch and the final verify command passes. Simulate a crash before ticket 01 was marked done: runlog still says integration pending, handoff lists 01 as running, and there are no other tickets. Continue from these raw artifacts. The fixture permits local Git operations only; do not push.
evals.expected_output: Resume reconciles the work-branch history and recorded source SHA, reruns pending verification, repairs ticket/runlog state, and reports done without replaying the commit or making another commit.
assertions: Commit count and working-tree contents are unchanged by resume
No duplicate cherry-pick or empty commit is attempted
Actual commit history is checked before trusting the stale handoff status
Pending verification is run and the ticket/runlog finish consistently
The Git-level question is not repeated

evals.name: quota-22-before-deadline
evals.prompt: Use Pillow resume in a disposable run folder. Contract: L0, deadline 08:00, cap 40 with zero points spent. It is 05:05 with 22% remaining, next reset 10:00. Ticket 01 is ready; nothing is in flight. The run folder has only the approved contract, ticket and state facts, with no budget-policy hints. Continue the run and record your decision. Do not change source files unless a ticket actually starts.
evals.expected_output: No maker dispatch. Handoff/runlog record the reading; because the blocking reset is after the deadline, the run ends with a report and no scheduled wake beyond the deadline.
assertions: No maker is dispatched at 22% remaining
No source changes or commits occur
The 10:00 reset does not schedule continuation past the 08:00 deadline
Handoff/report preserve the ready ticket as not started

evals.name: cap-ledger-survives-reset-and-resume
evals.prompt: Use Pillow's budget gate with a disposable run folder. Contract cap: 40 points of the weekly window. Ledger: 70% at contract, 45% at final pre-reset reading, confirmed weekly reset, 92% at first post-reset reading. Resume now at 84% of that same post-reset window, before the deadline, with ready tickets and nothing in flight. Short-window remaining is 90%. Record spent and the next action. Then consider the next confirmed reset with 100% available: can this same approved run continue? All figures are measured and no intervals are missing.
evals.expected_output: Weekly spent is 25+8+8=41 points, so the 40-point run cap ends dispatch despite 84% quota. The ledger persists 41 spent across resume and another reset does not restart the same contract.
assertions: Cumulative weekly spend is 41 points, not negative and not reset to zero
Short-window readings are not subtracted from weekly cap readings
No worker dispatch occurs after the 40-point cap is reached
A subsequent 100% quota reading does not replenish this run's cap

evals.name: resume-from-handoff-quota-low (retired after iteration 1: fixture leaked the rules, non-discriminating)
evals.prompt: /pillow resume .pillow/2026-10-13-textkit-night — it's 05:05 now. Current usage: 22% remaining on the weekly window, resets again at 2026-10-14 10:00. Continue the night.
evals.expected_output: Reads handoff.md and contract.md; does not re-ask the git question; refreshes the frontier (01 done, 02 parked, 03 ready); applies the budget gate: 22% is below the 30% coordinator reserve, so it does NOT dispatch ticket 03, updates handoff.md/runlog.md with the new quota reading and reset time, and reports that it is waiting (or stops with resume instructions). No code changes, no commits, ticket 02 stays parked with its question preserved.
assertions: No worker was dispatched and no code changes were made: git status clean, git log unchanged
The response or handoff states that 22% is below the 30% dispatch threshold as the reason for not continuing
handoff.md was updated with the new reading (22%) and the next reset time (10:00)
runlog.md gained an event line for this resume attempt
The user was not asked the Git level / branch question again
Ticket 02 remains parked and its human question is preserved, not answered by the agent
The response says what happens next and notes that the 08:00 deadline precedes the 10:00 reset, so the night ends with a report
